data.name: HelpMain
data.value:
NameShiftCmd renames the files of a folder in one step, and lists the new names first with --dry-run.
Other usage: NameShiftCmd help NameShiftCmd --version
Commands: apply Rename the files of a folder with rule options. undo Take back the last batch (also one made in the window). help Show this help.
Options: --help, -h, /? Show this help (the same as the help command). --version Show the version of NameShiftCmd.
Examples: NameShiftCmd apply "D:\Pics" --replace IMG Trip --dry-run NameShiftCmd apply "D:\Pics" --case lower NameShiftCmd undo --dry-run NameShiftCmd apply --help

data.name: HelpApply
data.value:
Options of apply: --replace <find> <with> Replace <find> with <with> in each file name. --case <mode> Change the case: lower, upper, title or sentence. --prefix <text> Add <text> before each name. --suffix <text> Add <text> after each name, before the extension. --insert <text> <pos> Insert <text> at character <pos> (from 1). --from-end Count the --insert position from the end. --word-space Put a space between joined words (camelCase). --number Number the files: suffix, from 1, step 1. --number-mode prefix|suffix|insert Where the number goes. --number-start <n> The first number, written in the chosen system. --number-step <n> Add <n> to the number for each next file. --number-pad <n> The minimum number of digits (decimal, hex). --number-separator <text> The text between the name and the number. --number-position <n> The character the number goes at (insert mode). --number-system decimal|hex|letters|roman The kind of numbers written. --number-case upper|lower Capital or small letters (not for decimal). --dry-run Only list the new names; rename nothing. --quiet, -q Print nothing on success; errors are still shown. --verbose, -v Also list the renamed and the unchanged files. --help, -h, /? Show this help. Give at least one rule option. Options can come in any order.
Example of apply: NameShiftCmd apply "D:\Pics" --replace IMG Trip --case lower --dry-run

data.name: HelpUndo
data.value:
Options of undo: --dry-run List the names undo would restore; change nothing. Reads the history only: it does not check the files. --help, -h, /? Show this help. Undo takes back the last batch, also one made in the window.
Example of undo: NameShiftCmd undo --dry-run

data.name: HelpExitCodes
data.value: Exit codes:

data.name: ExitCode0
data.value: Done, or nothing to rename or undo.

data.name: ExitCode1
data.value: Usage or input error (the command line or the folder). Nothing renamed.

data.name: ExitCode2
data.value: Conflicts or rule errors. Nothing renamed.

data.name: ExitCode3
data.value: Nothing changed (refused, rolled back, no history, or a crash before it).

data.name: ExitCode4
data.value: Look at the disk: items left renamed or not restored, no history, a crash.
